articles.t: GTA 6 fait un carnage : Call of Duty, Fortnite et EA FC 27 perdent des millions de joueurs
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 ne se contente pas de battre des records de ventes : son lancement aurait aussi provoqué une chute spectaculaire de la fréquentation de Call of Duty, Fortnite et EA FC 27. Et avec l'arrivée prochaine de GTA Online, le plus dur pourrait encore être à venir pour ses concurrents.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 ne se contente pas de battre des records de ventes : son lancement aurait aussi provoqué une chute spectaculaire de la fréquentation de Call of Duty, Fortnite et EA FC 27. Et avec l’arrivée prochaine de GTA Online, le plus dur pourrait encore être à venir pour ses concurrents.
Grand Theft Auto VI se serait vendu à 44,9 millions d’exemplaires à la fin de son week-end de lancement, d’après un rapport d’Alinea Analytics publié sur Substack. Le cabinet indique aussi que 40,8 millions de joueurs ont lancé le jeu dimanche 22 novembre.
Vendredi, Take-Two Interactive et Rockstar Games avaient communiqué leurs premiers résultats : 32,5 millions de copies en précommandes et 3,79 milliards de dollars de revenus générés jusqu’au 19 novembre, jour du lancement.
Alinea Analytics fournit pour sa part une estimation de l’évolution des ventes depuis. Selon le cabinet, les 44,9 millions de copies correspondent à des ventes effectives, et ne comptent donc pas les stocks encore invendus chez les distributeurs.
Sur ce total, 33,7 millions d’exemplaires auraient été vendus sur PlayStation 5, contre 11,2 millions sur Xbox Series S et X. Cette répartition de 75 % et 25 % confirme une proportion déjà mesurée par Sensor Tower.
Alinea estime par ailleurs que les revenus bruts dépassent « largement » les 4 milliards de dollars. Le cabinet rapproche ce montant des recettes cumulées des deux plus gros succès de l’année au cinéma : Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2,5 milliards de dollars) et The Odyssey (1,8 milliard). Il y voit une confirmation de l’affirmation de l’éditeur, qui présente ce lancement comme le plus important de l’histoire du divertissement.
Pour la PlayStation 5 , Alinea détaille la répartition géographique des joueurs. Plus de 32,8 % d’entre eux se trouvent aux États-Unis. Viennent ensuite la France (9 %), le Royaume-Uni (7,3 %), l’Allemagne (5,1 %) et la Chine (4,7 %).
Le rapport s’intéresse aussi à l’impact de la sortie sur d’autres titres, mesuré en nombre d’utilisateurs actifs quotidiens :
L’analyste Rhys Elliott souligne que ces chiffres concernent uniquement la partie solo de GTA VI. Selon lui, le retour à la normale après le lancement de la nouvelle version de GTA Online, dont la date n’est pas précisée, sera probablement plus difficile pour ces jeux en service continu.

articles.t: GTA 6 vient de sortir son premier patch, qu’est ce qu’il change ?
articles.chapeau: Quatre jours après sa sortie, GTA 6 demande déjà un nouveau téléchargement sur consoles avec son tout premier patch.
articles.txt:
Quatre jours après sa sortie, GTA 6 demande déjà un nouveau téléchargement sur consoles avec son tout premier patch.
GTA 6 est sorti le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X/S, et le jeu n’en était déjà pas à sa première mise à jour. Avant même le lancement, Rockstar avait poussé deux patchs obligatoires pour les copies préchargées. Le premier date du 13 novembre et pesait 1,07 Go sur PS5 et 2,18 Go sur Xbox, le second est arrivé le 16 novembre. Depuis la sortie, plusieurs joueurs signalent aussi des plantages, donc on attendait tous un correctif rapide.
Seulement, voici le premier patch après la sortie du jeu. Les consoles proposent la version 01.002.002 de GTA 6. Elle pèse 603 Mo sur PS5 et environ 1,6 Go sur Xbox Series X/S . Comme pour les patchs précédents, Rockstar la déploie par vagues : en début de journée, seul un tiers des joueurs PS5 pouvait la télécharger, et le reste doit suivre dans les heures qui viennent. Si vous ne la voyez pas encore, c’est normal.
Rockstar n’a publié aucun patchnote pour le moment. On n’a rien trouvé sur le Newswire ni sur la page d’assistance du studio. On imagine qu’il s’agit surtout de correctifs techniques après le lancement, mais pour l’instant, ça reste une supposition.
Sur les réseaux, certains affirment que la mise à jour corrige le glitch d’argent de la grange de Hamlet qui permettait de récupérer 10 000 dollars facilement après chaque sauvegarde. Rien ne le confirme officiellement, donc on prend ça avec des pincettes. Les joueurs espèrent surtout voir disparaître le plantage avec le code d’erreur CE-108255-1 sur PS5 . Certains restent bloqués dans la mission « Pipework » au moment de prendre la ventouse, et d’autres ne dépassent même pas le prologue sur PS5 Pro. Vider le cache ou reconstruire la base de données ne semble pas suffire, et Sony se contente de conseiller de mettre le jeu à jour.
On mettra cet article à jour dès que Rockstar publiera le patchnote.
Sur PS5, sélectionnez GTA 6 sur l’écran d’accueil, appuyez sur la touche Options puis choisissez « Rechercher une mise à jour ». Si rien n’apparaît, c’est que votre console ne fait pas encore partie de la vague en cours. Sur Xbox Series X/S, passez par « Mes jeux et applications », puis « Gérer » et « Mises à jour ». GTA 6 s’y affiche dès que le patch est disponible pour vous.

articles.t: GTA 6's First Official Post-Release Update Has A Catch
articles.chapeau: Rockstar is handling GTA 6's updates very differently than what players may be used to on major PS5 and Xbox games
articles.txt:
It hasn't quite been a whole week since the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 , but the game already has an update to download. Here's what you need to know about Rockstar's update for the open-world game and how it differs between PlayStation 5 and Xbox platforms.
The official update is version 01.002.002, and its size differs depending on console: on PS5, it's 603.8 MB, whereas the Xbox version is much larger at 1.6 GB​​​​​​​ . However, there are two major things to note about the update.​​​​​​​
Much like the pre-launch updates , this new patch will roll out in stages throughout Nov. 23​​​​​​​ . So if you log into the game, check to see if there's something to download — but don't fret if nothing is there yet. Your update should appear or start downloading automatically at some point on Monday.
The other thing worth noting is that Rockstar has not yet published​​​​​​​ any patch notes. Players have made various claims about what the update includes, such as a fix for the infinite money glitch , a toned-down vignette feature, and possible changes to the game's autosave .​​​​​​​ There is no shortage of things players hope Rockstar will address, like the annoyances of selecting a specific amount of money while interacting with ATMs or BuckMe . Critically, no specific changes have been confirmed yet.
What's unlikely to change is the game's weather system. Rockstar made a big deal about the dynamic weather system prior to launch, but fans playing through the game have come to believe the feature is bugged​​​​​​​ . Some fans have been playing for many hours and have yet to see thunderstorms, for instance, which seems unusual for a game set in a place known for its microclimates. The feature is tied to your progression in the game, according to Rockstar.

articles.t: Un bug permet de jouer à GTA 6 à 60 fps (mais ne testez pas)
articles.chapeau: Sur Xbox Series X et Series S, GTA 6 permet une manipulation qui débloque le framerate, au-delà des 30 images par seconde. On a testé, et on ne recommande pas du tout. Avant le lancement de GTA 6, disponible depuis le 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X, Rockstar Games avait donné, le 10 novembre,
articles.txt:
Recevez tous les soirs un résumé de l’actu importante avec Le Récap’
Avant le lancement de GTA 6 , disponible depuis le 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X, Rockstar Games avait donné, le 10 novembre, quelques détails techniques sur le jeu. On a alors appris une mauvaise nouvelle : GTA 6 vise les 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles , même la plus puissante (la PS5 Pro). Même pas de mode 40 fps pour gagner un peu de confort . Rockstar Games justifie ce choix par le niveau de détail qu’il veut garder dans Leonida, des décors aux personnages qui les peuplent.
Fort heureusement, les 30 images par seconde proposées par GTA 6 sont correctement gérées, avec un rendu vraiment optimisé par Rockstar Games. Le titre, pourtant immense, est très beau et tient bien ses 30 images par seconde. Pour les adeptes de la fluidité à tout prix, il existe un bug pour débloquer le framerate. Numerama l’a testé, et on le déconseille.
GTA VI // Source : Rockstar Games La version Xbox de GTA 6 peut dépasser les 30 fps, mais… Ce bug touche la version Xbox de GTA 6 , et ne fonctionne que si la console est reliée à un téléviseur compatible 120 Hz. Découvert sur Xbox Series X, il marche aussi sur Xbox Series S, comme l’a montré la chaîne Fuzion Xbox Testing, relayée par Pure Xbox . Il a été repéré sur la version 01.002.001 de GTA 6 , toujours la plus récente ce lundi 23 novembre, et une future mise à jour pourrait le corriger.
Le bug exploite la fonction Quick Resume, qui permet de mettre plusieurs jeux en suspens, et de reprendre sa partie quasi immédiatement (même après avoir débranché la console).
En lançant la partie, vous remarquerez tout de suite le gain en fluidité, même s’il est irrégulier (entre 45 et 90 fps). Seulement voilà, toutes les animations sont accélérées, que ce soit les mouvements des personnages ou ceux des véhicules. Tout porte à croire que la vitesse du jeu est indexée sur le framerate. En somme, si le framerate augmente, la vitesse du jeu aussi. Sur Reddit, Meowwie64 , le joueur qui a découvert la manipulation, indique que les cinématiques, elles, gardent leur vitesse normale, et le montre dans un clip . Il précise aussi que la manipulation, quand elle rate, peut à l’inverse bloquer le jeu à 15 fps.
Pour revenir à la normale, il suffit de quitter complètement GTA 6 depuis le menu de la console, puis de le relancer : le jeu retrouve son plafond de 30 images par seconde.
Ce phénomène rappelle un bug de Dark Souls 2 sur PC : à 60 fps, les armes s’usaient deux fois plus vite qu’à 30 fps, car leur usure était liée au framerate. FromSoftware n’a corrigé le problème que bien plus tard, sur PC comme sur la réédition Scholar of the First Sin .

articles.t: I benched my gaming PC for Grand Theft Auto 6 on Xbox Series S. Here
articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6 is here for consoles, leaving my PC useless. What
articles.txt:
Click for next article (Image credit: Rockstar Games | Microsoft) Jump To: The Bad Stuff The Good Stuff The Honest Truth {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Bluesky Threads Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launched on November 19 , and as expected, it's a cultural event that's capturing the gaming world's interest and making even non-gamers sit back and wonder what they're looking at.
When the game's reviews went live — including our own five-star review from Jez Corden — I knew that there was no way I could miss out on the fun of discovering an unexplored open world of this scale.
Just one problem. The gaming PC into which I've poured thousands of dollars is useless. No one knows when GTA 6 is actually coming to PC in an official capacity (barring some sketchy AI recompiles).
Not wanting to spend another $1,000+ on a Series X or PS5 just to play one game, I picked up an unused Xbox Series S my brother had lying around.
I thought I knew what I was getting myself into. I'd seen Digital Foundry's breakdown of performance on all consoles, including less-than-great results for the Series S. I know that the game runs at a maximum of 30 FPS no matter the console, a far cry from the 200+ FPS to which I'm accustomed on my PC.
About 30-40 hours of marathon gaming later (who needs sleep?), I'm ready to be brutally honest about what it's like going from PC to Series S for GTA 6 .
Disclaimer All Grand Theft Auto 6 images and videos in this article was captured on an Xbox Series S, unless otherwise stated.
Usually, if I see 30 FPS while gaming, I assume that something's wrong with my PC. On the Series S, 30 FPS is more of a goal than a baseline .
Despite running at a 720p native resolution that's then upscaled to 1080p with AMD's FSR 4 tech running behind the scenes, the Series S has a hard time remaining at 30 FPS when the action picks up.
👉 Xbox Series S FINALLY gets the respect it deserves — all thanks to GTA 6
Frame rates seem to move around quite freely between 20 and 30 FPS on the Series S when things get frenetic. It's a tough sell, to be sure, but at least everything feels a lot smoother when you're just cruising around and checking out the game's seemingly endless supply of content.
As a PC gamer, comparing performance at 20 to 30 FPS feels a bit like asking which piece of trash on the ground is least soggy . It's still going to feel gross, but at least you have something .
The Xbox Series X , PS5 , and PS5 Pro do at least bump the resolution up to 1440p , which is then upscaled to 4K , providing a sharper overall picture.
Am I regretting playing at the Series S's 720p resolution upscaled to 1080p, shown on a big 4K TV? Not at all.
I'm used to precision controls without input latency. Switching to a gamepad on a console running at 30 FPS or less makes me feel like I've already had a full case of Pindayho cold ones while seated on my couch.
Driving and shooting, two of the game's primary activities, take a lot of getting used to because of input latency .
Good news, though. By the end of my first marathon session, I'd basically stopped noticing input latency at all. I'm no longer regularly crashing my car or whiffing shots because of it. Back to blaming my own abilities with a gamepad.
I don't think I'll ever get used to the game's abysmal frame rate, but at least the input lag irons itself out in my brain. Oh, yeah, and don't forget that all consoles suffer from similar latency.
The first 10 hours of GTA 6 have me believing the game's stellar reviews. Despite using the weakest console to run it at a lower resolution, it's one of the most detailed and visually impressive games I've ever seen.

articles.t: Hacker jailed for seven years after leaking GTA 6 clips
articles.chapeau: A criminal who hacked into the makers of Grand Theft Auto and leaked clips of the highly anticipated game as part of a string of cyberattacks has been jailed for seven years.
articles.txt: 0 Comments --> 2 Hacker jailed for seven years after leaking GTA 6 clips Arion Kurtaj (Image: City of London Police / PA) Hacker jailed for seven years after leaking GTA 6 clips A person playing Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) (Image: Yui Mok/Press Association) 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A criminal who hacked into the makers of Grand Theft Auto and leaked clips of the highly anticipated game as part of a string of cyberattacks has been jailed for seven years. Arion Kurtaj, 21 and from Oxford, a member of the cybercrime group Lapsus$, hacked into Rockstar Games, the makers of the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) franchise, and took 90 gameplay videos from the highly anticipated GTA VI. He then subsequently released the clips online under the pseudonym TeaPotUberHacker, and threatened to release the game’s source code. The defendant appeared at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, where he was sentenced to seven years in prison, having previously pleaded guilty to a charge of fraud and offences under the Computer Misuse Act. Kurtaj has already spent time in custody, so he walked free from court on Monday. READ MORE: Stalker, who sent threatening messages to influencer, jailed A person playing Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) (Image: Yui Mok/Press Association) Sentencing him, Mr Justice Turner said: “You are obviously a very talented young man. “Don’t waste those talents by spending the rest of your life in and out of prison.” Kurtaj stood in the glass dock wearing a white shirt and black suit jacket. The cyberattacks took place between August 2021 and September 2022. Kurtaj hacked into the servers and data files of broadband provider BT and mobile operator EE between August and November 2021. In early November that year, BT noticed an increase in unauthorised Sim swaps of their customers’ mobile phones, said to be rooted in the defendant’s initial hack. According to the CPS, Sim swapping allows criminals to trick providers into switching phone numbers to a new Sim card, letting them take control of victims’ calls and texts and giving them access to bank or social media accounts. The then-teenager was charged in relation to the offences, but kept carrying out similar attacks after being moved to a hotel for his own protection in September 2022, using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick. He also accessed financial technology firm Revolut’s systems, compromising thousands of customers’ information. And in a separate attack on Uber, he sent a lewd image to employees, exfiltrated sensitive data, and deleted data and accounts from internal systems. This resulted in costs in excess of 2.8 million dollars (£2.1 million) to the transportation company. The defendant was initially arrested and remanded in custody in September 2022. He was charged with 12 offences but following medical assessment, he was deemed unfit to plead. A jury found after a trial at Southwark Crown Court in August 2023 that Kurtaj had committed the offences and he was given a hospital order in December that year. Following a further assessment in 2025, Kurtaj was found fit to plead and the CPS decided to reinstate proceedings. Last week he pleaded guilty to three counts of an unauthorised act to impair the operation of a computer, one count of fraud, one count of securing unauthorised access to computer material with intent and one count of possession of a mobile phone in prison. He also admitted two counts of assaulting an emergency worker. GTA VI is estimated to have raked in almost £2 billion since its debut and is thought to be the biggest entertainment launch in history. The latest instalment in Rockstar’s blockbuster video game series became available to UK users at midnight on Thursday, ending a 13-year wait since the franchise’s previous instalment.

articles.t: Clearing Up False Info About The ‘GTA 6’ Criminal Profile System
articles.chapeau: 'GTA 6' has a new cirminal profile system that tracks your violent actions, but players believe they need to be way more careful than they need to.
articles.txt:
One of the most controversial aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6 among players has been a spin on Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system, called a Criminal Profile. New to the GTA franchise, in this more grounded game, it measures your capacity for violence, essentially ranging from "only what is necessary" (and a lot is necessary) to blind rampages. The system is a bit confusing, and now people attempting to reach certain endings unlockable through specific profiles are being fed misinformation online, so here's how it really works. First, here are the levels:
Once you get to Irredeemable, you can never lower your rating again. And boy, does it take a lot to get to Irredeemable.
There is a concern among players that, in order to maintain a low criminal profile and be on track for a better ending (it does come into play), they have to go way, way out of their way to handicap themselves to get there. But that isn't true.
After 150 hours, I have never once gone out of my way to incapacitate enemies with non-lethal limb shots instead of never aiming for the head or heart. I found pretty quickly that A) shooting an automatic weapon at enemies is not really going to discriminate and B) for stealth runs I need people dead, not rolling around yelling.
This has never, ever taken my overall criminal profile level above Hardened. And despite some claims, to qualify for the "good" ending, you can still be Hardened, and you do not need to be Professional tier.
Where you get the most Professional points in the game is by getting in and out of robberies and heists covertly, or at least by maintaining good crowd control without needing to hurt anyone. This is good for just…gameplay reasons, as it's way easier to escape with the money and loot if you do not walk in guns blazing, setting off the alarm immediately.
Furthermore, if you are fighting actual enemies like in missions or in any of the gang hideouts, you are not getting "purple devil points" for killing them. You only get those if there is an injured enemy on the ground and you go out of your way to execute them.
You will get instant purple devil points if you shoot cops in the open world or unarmed civilians not attacking you. But shooting a few cops to escape isn't going to do much, as you really have to go on lengthy police shootouts killing a lot of them to start moving the needle. Even then, to really move down the list requires not just that but civilian rampages and getting to Irredeemable? You need to be doing those a lot. Like you really, really have to go out of your way.
You can debate the existence of the entire system, but I think players should know that maintaining a low profile, no higher than Hardened, does not need to be some sort of gameplay-crippling task. So, hit those headshots if you want.
Pick up my sci-fi novels the Herokiller series and The Earthborn Trilogy .

articles.t: Pourquoi GTA 6 est meilleur sur PS5, et pourquoi ce n'est pas une question de performances
articles.chapeau: La manette DualSense, ses gâchettes adaptatives et ses moteurs de vibration forment peut-être l'atout secret de la PlayStation 5 pour GTA 6 face à la Xbox Series X.
articles.txt: Le verdict est tombé : entre les versions PS5 "standard" et la Xbox Series X , GTA 6 fait jeu égal sur les performances techniques. Mais s'il y a bien un facteur différenciant entre les deux consoles de 2020, c'est l'utilisation de leurs manettes respectives. Si la manette de Microsoft ne profite d'aucune particularité technique, nonobstant sa qualité intrinsèque, la DualSense de la PS5 est ici grandement exploitée, en particulier ses moteurs haptiques et ses gâchettes adaptatives. Le diable est dans les détails, a fortiori sur un jeu aussi méticuleux que GTA 6 , et force est de constater que Rockstar a apporté un soin tout particulier au pad de Sony.

articles.t: GTA 6 reçoit déjà une nouvelle mise à jour avec des changements attendus par les joueurs
articles.chapeau: Quatre jours après la sortie de GTA 6, Rockstar pousse déjà la mise à jour 01.002.002 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Entre crashs, sauvegardes et glitches, les joueurs espèrent un tournant sans encore savoir ce qui change vraiment.
articles.txt:
Quatre jours après la sortie de GTA 6, Rockstar pousse déjà la mise à jour 01.002.002 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Entre crashs, sauvegardes et glitches, les joueurs espèrent un tournant sans encore savoir ce qui change vraiment.
À peine quatre jours après la sortie de GTA 6 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S , un nouveau patch commence déjà à tomber. Numérotée 01.002.002 sur PS5 (1.0.2.2 côté Xbox), cette mise à jour surprend par sa rapidité et relance immédiatement une question chez les joueurs : est-ce que Rockstar Games commence enfin à corriger les crashs, les sauvegardes capricieuses et les glitches qui font le tour des réseaux ?
Officiellement, silence radio. Aucune note de patch n’a été publiée, ni pour cette version, ni pour les deux mises à jour pré-lancement. Mais entre les dataminers et les premiers retours de la communauté, on commence à voir se dessiner le vrai visage de cette 01.002.002, que beaucoup espèrent déjà cruciale pour profiter sereinement de Leonida avec Jason et Lucia.
Selon le compte X PlayStation Game Size et le dataminer Tex2 , la mise à jour 01.002.002 pèse environ 603 Mo sur PS5 et autour de 1,6 Go sur Xbox Series X|S. L’analyse des fichiers montre surtout des changements côté exécutable, scripts et shaders, sans ajout de contenu visible ni nouvelle zone de carte. Tout indique donc un patch essentiellement technique, centré sur la stabilité et les performances.
Problème : Rockstar Games ne détaille rien. Impossible de dire officiellement quels bugs sont corrigés. Sur le subreddit dédié à GTA 6 , les joueurs testent donc par eux-mêmes. Le glitch de vue à la première personne , par exemple, est toujours actif après la mise à jour. L’utilisateur « TheRealKillerFish » confirme qu’en jonglant avec le pavé tactile et le smartphone en jeu, il est encore possible de forcer une caméra façon FPS, alors que cette option n’existe pas dans les menus.
Sur PS5 , la priorité reste les crashs fréquents, parfois accompagnés du code d’erreur CE-108255-1. Plusieurs témoignages évoquent un retour brutal au menu et une reprise sur une sauvegarde bien plus ancienne, à cause d’un système d’autosave jugé trop limité. En attendant d’avoir la certitude que la 01.002.002 règle ce point, la recommandation reste claire : multiplier les sauvegardes manuelles.
Côté Xbox Series X|S , les joueurs pointent surtout un Quick Resume capricieux , qui ralentit le jeu ou bricole le frame rate après une reprise de session. S’ajoutent des soucis de lock-on et un shimmering graphique sur certains écrans. Autre dossier brûlant, les différents money glitchs qui font flamber l’économie du jeu, clairement dans le viseur de Rockstar même si rien ne confirme encore leur disparition avec ce patch.
La mise à jour a commencé à être déployée le 23 novembre 2026, soit seulement quatre jours après la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Sur PS5, le déploiement se fait par vagues : environ 33 % des joueurs sont servis immédiatement, 66 % au bout de quelques heures, puis l’ensemble de la base dans un délai d’environ six heures. Sur Xbox, le patch semble proposé de manière plus globale.
Pour vérifier manuellement, il suffit de sélectionner le jeu sur PS5, d’appuyer sur Options puis « Vérifier les mises à jour ». Sur Xbox, passez par « Gérer le jeu » puis la section mises à jour. Aucune version PC n’existant pour l’instant, seuls les joueurs console sont concernés. Avec trois patches en une dizaine de jours, Rockstar montre qu’il surveille de près son blockbuster, même si l’absence totale de patch notes laisse à la communauté le soin de dire si cette 01.002.002 rend enfin vos virées à Leonida plus stables. Alors, avez-vous encore des crashs après l’installation ?

According to the CPS, Sim swapping allows criminals to trick providers into switching phone numbers to a new Sim card, letting them take control of victims’ calls and texts and giving them access to bank or social media accounts.
The then-teenager was charged in relation to the offences, but kept carrying out similar attacks after being moved to a hotel for his own protection in September 2022, using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick.
He also accessed financial technology firm Revolut’s systems, compromising thousands of customers’ information.
And in a separate attack on Uber, he sent a lewd image to employees, exfiltrated sensitive data, and deleted data and accounts from internal systems.
This resulted in costs in excess of 2.8 million dollars (£2.1 million) to the transportation company.
The defendant, formerly of Oxfordshire , was initially arrested and remanded in custody in September 2022.
He was charged with 12 offences but following medical assessment, he was deemed unfit to plead.
A jury found after a trial at Southwark Crown Court in August 2023 that Kurtaj had committed the offences and he was given a hospital order in December that year.
Following a further assessment in 2025, Kurtaj was found fit to plead and the CPS decided to reinstate proceedings.
Last week he pleaded guilty to three counts of an unauthorised act to impair the operation of a computer, one count of fraud, one count of securing unauthorised access to computer material with intent and one count of possession of a mobile phone in prison.
He also admitted two counts of assaulting an emergency worker.
GTA VI is estimated to have raked in almost £2 billion since its debut and is thought to be the biggest entertainment launch in history.
The latest instalment in Rockstar’s blockbuster video game series became available to UK users at midnight on Thursday, ending a 13-year wait since the franchise’s previous instalment.

articles.t: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'
articles.chapeau: 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and others he carried out when he was a teenager.
articles.txt:
Share Save Add as preferred on Google Joe Tidy Cyber correspondent, World Service, Woolwich Crown Court City of London Police During the trial, the prosecution described Kurtaj as a "leading light" in the teen gang Lapsus$ A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence after serving the majority of a seven-year sentence.
Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, was released from custody with the judge warning him: "Don't let this happen again."
The now 21-year-old hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022.
Kurtaj had pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.
Kurtaj was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.
But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.
He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years. It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord.
City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".
He hacked Rockstar games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester.
He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.
With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.
He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."
The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.
Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.
The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.
He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.
The Judge Mr Justice Turner told him "you are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again."
Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people.
"The restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist," they said.
They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to "people who were involved in hacking".
During the pandemic, he was "very isolated" and his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously," they added.
Kurtaj and the gang's other hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber used social engineering techniques - tricking people into clicking malicious links or giving up sensitive information - to gain access to internal systems.
Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.
His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.
Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.
The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 (£230,000) from individual victims.
Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.
In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

articles.t: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Is Being Review Bombed On Metacritic
GTA 6 After Launch Weekend: Is It as Good as Players Expected?
articles.chapeau: A solid follow-up to GTA 5 or a "boyfriend simulator"?
articles.txt:
Behind The Incredible New Tech and Systems Rockstar Built to Make GTA 6 Feel Alive
GTA 6 has been released, and it's safe to say it is the most anticipated release of the last decade. According to Sensor Tower's data , the game's pre-orders have generated $751 million, with 7.71 million copies sold. Analysts suggested the long-awaited GTA follow-up might sell over 25 million copies on launch day and earn $7.6 billion in the first two months.
Demand was so high that PlayStation Network confirmed a service disruption on Wednesday, November 18, hours before the game's release. The game didn't disappoint: just after launch, it received some of the strongest review scores in video game history and held a 99 average on Metacritic . It had reportedly generated approximately $1.84 billion in sales revenue by its release day.
Soon after the release, Rockstar Games announced that GTA 6 also sold 32.5 million units before its November 19 release, establishing a new pre-release record across all platforms. GTA 6 has officially delivered the biggest entertainment launch in history , generating an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales during its first 24 hours.
Now that the first weekend is over and many players have explored Vice City, we can get a fuller picture of how players perceive the game. As of writing, the game still holds a 99 Metascore , with a user score sitting at 5.6. Player reviews range from delighted 10/10s that call it the best game of all time and praise its story, graphics, and classic GTA features, to average and low scores. Among the shortcomings, players mainly cite the 30 FPS cap . Some say relationship-building and chores should be optional, calling the game a "boyfriend simulator."
"30 FPS, Console Exclusive, Restricted freedom and uninteresting characters are a no go for a 13 year development cycle."
"I had the highest expectations for GTA 6, and so I reasonably didn't expect the game to meet a third of them. It's beyond crazy that I can, without a doubt, say that this game has exceeded my lofty expectations. Besides the 30fps, there's literally nothing I don't like about this game."
"GTA 6 is nothing short of a masterpiece. Rockstar Games has outdone themselves once again, delivering an absolutely brilliant experience that sets a new benchmark for open-world gaming. The attention to detail, the breathtaking visuals of Leonida, and the deeply engaging storyline keep you completely hooked from start to finish. The world feels incredibly alive, dynamic, and chaotic in the best way possible. It is pure genius, a thrilling ride, and easily an instant classic. A flawless 10/10."
"This game is so woke can't believe they're trying to teach me how to be in a relationship."
There are claims that GTA 6 is being "review-bombed," with dozens of negative player reviews appearing within a few hours, and some of them reportedly come from Zelda fans.
Rockstar had already hinted at a shift in tone, drawing on Red Dead Redemption 2, whose protagonist comes to regret his violent life. Besides the romantic relationship at the center of the story, Rockstar's Rob Nelson said the game, in some sense, encourages more empathetic, kind player behavior .

articles.t: What if I don't like Grand Theft Auto? | TheSixthAxis
articles.chapeau: Am I out of touch? No, it's the children who are wrong.
articles.txt:
What if I don’t like Grand Theft Auto? That’s the question that’s been skulking like a criminal into my subconscious over this past week. I’ve spent my entire life gaming, played every major franchise under the sun – and a few minor ones too – but Grand Theft Auto has never really been for me. It’s never given me much pain or caused too much soul-searching over the decades, but here, with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI , and what feels like a pivotal moment in gaming, I’ve never felt more at odds with myself. Am I missing out? Am I plain wrong?
Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest entertainment property in the world in terms of financial clout. Captain America commiserates with Harry Potter, Luke Skywalker heads back to that lonely island where he hid from Rey, and Mickey Mouse looks longingly – though obviously cheerfully – at its success. No other single property has made as much money in as short a space of time. Ever. That’s truly an incredible achievement, and even more so for a Scottish company that’s grown into a worldwide behemoth.
As cultural touchstones go, it’s clear that Grand Theft Auto, and especially Grand Theft Auto VI, is as valid and essential to modern culture as those iconic franchises. You only have to scroll through social media to see how big it is, with memes, easter eggs and storylines spinning out a global shorthand for its impact, and for all of the successes of other games, movies and TV shows, there’s few, if any, that have given me FOMO in quite the same way as GTA 6 .
Why don’t I like these games? I’ll tell anyone who’ll listen that I’ve always played games to be the hero, the victor, the plumber who rescues the princess from the castle. I’ve never once felt the desire to be the bad guy, outside of being a horrible goose, and in games where I’ve had the choice – Fable, Mass Effect, et al – I’ve always played like the biggest boy scout in the world, running around fixing everyone’s problems. I’m sure that psychologically says something very obvious about me – my upbringing, my fear of rejection, of failure, of not being accepted – but I’ve never found joy in running riot over anything, whether it’s digital, or not.
The last time I played Grand Theft Auto was GTA 4. I found it interesting enough to start with, and the tech behind it was definitely impressive, but the story soon forced me to do something I simply didn’t want to: stab a man to death. I don’t fully know why GTA feels different to a million other games where you hack, slash or stab at the enemy in front of you, but there’s a layer of realism that Rockstar has achieved that breaks the digital distance down. To me, the freedom, the opportunity to cause chaos and destruction is, in fact, a constraint. I don’t want to do those things in real life. I guess I don’t want to do them in a digital life, either.
Of course, there is a lot more to GTA 6 than just raiding gang hideouts, pulling off heists and committing petty crimes. I could go and scout out all of the wildlife that has been recreated for the game, I could indulge in fashion and kitting out fast cars, get myself rescued by a dog on a jetski, and all manner of other activities, but underneath it all is that crime story.
I know that everything isn’t for everyone. It shouldn’t be. GTA 6, though, is so big, so important to gaming in general, that as a fan of gaming, I need to understand it; I need to experience it so that I can be a part of the conversation. Rockstar has limited that by making GTA 6 the first huge franchise entry to go all-digital.
I’d have given in, bought the disc, played ten hours to revel in the animation, the graphics, the storytelling, and then likely decided it still wasn’t for me. I’d have popped down to CEX, or posted it to eBay, and that would have been the end of my GTA 6 adventure. As it stands, I can pay full price – a very premium £70 – for a game I don’t really want to keep, or I can stay out of the conversation. I guess that’s another kind of cultural moment.
GTA 6 is unlikely to be bettered for a long time. The scale, the cost, and the length of time that’s gone into its production are resources that few studios, if any, will ever sustain again, especially with the rise of AI tools. It’s clearly remarkable – games don’t get to sit atop decades’ worth of other exceptional creations if they’re not – and it’s built on the foundations of what was already one of the world’s most successful gaming franchises. C’est même un mal pour un bien puisqu’il rentrera plus facilement dans un setup restreint où le moindre espace compte toujours.
La livraison est offerte et Amazon affiche une possibilité de retour jusqu’au 15 janvier 2027. Vous disposez également de la garantie de deux ans en cas de panne ou défaut de conception. articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC en 60 FPS : voici la config à viser, en tour PC comme en PC portable — Frandroid
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 pulvérise tous les records sur console, mais il reste bloqué à 30 images par seconde. Pour doubler la mise sur PC dès sa sortie estimée
articles.txt:
Sur PS5 Pro , la console de salon la plus puissante du marché, Grand Theft Auto VI plafonne à 30 images par seconde, un résultat salué par les experts techniques de Digital Foundry . Après plus de 50 heures de jeu sans la moindre chute de cadence, le journaliste John Linneman évoque même « la meilleure façon de jouer à ce jeu, et de loin ».
Pour un joueur PC habitué à la fluidité du 60 ou du 144 images par seconde, ce plafond ressemble pourtant à un bond en arrière. Doubler le nombre d’images affichées va demander un investissement conséquent, mais pas forcément sur le composant que l’on imagine : sur PC aussi, la barre des 60 images par seconde sera difficile à atteindre , et la carte graphique n’est pas la première responsable.
Sony PlayStation 5 Pro Fiche produit Voir le test Disponible à 515 ,27 € Sony PlayStation 5 Slim Fiche produit Voir le test Disponible à 648 ,24 € 9 /10 Microsoft Xbox Series X Fiche produit Voir le test Disponible à 456 ,74 € Quand sortira GTA 6 sur PC ? Disponible depuis le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S uniquement, la sortie de GTA 6 a déjà affolé les compteurs avec plus de 17 millions d’exemplaires vendus avant même son lancement selon le cabinet Sensor Tower. Côté PC, Rockstar garde officiellement le silence et le patron de l’éditeur Take-Two, Strauss Zelnick, botte en touche en rappelant que « les informations viennent toujours de nos labels ».
Selon GamesBeat , qui s’appuie sur quatre sources proches du dossier, le portage PC viserait toutefois le premier trimestre 2027 (entre janvier et mars 2027, juste avant la clôture de l’exercice fiscal de Take-Two). Ce serait un délai record pour le studio : Rockstar avait fait patienter les joueurs PC 13 mois pour Red Dead Redemption 2 (sorti en octobre 2018 sur console, puis en novembre 2019 sur PC) et 19 mois pour GTA V sur la génération PS4/Xbox One.
Comme à son habitude, le studio devrait réserver cette version PC à une annonce séparée quelques mois avant le lancement, probablement accompagnée d’options graphiques exclusives (ray tracing étendu, distance d’affichage accrue) et d’une sortie d’abord centrée sur son propre Rockstar Games Launcher avant Steam et l’Epic Games Store. En attendant une officialisation à suivre dans notre suivi en direct de GTA 6 , il faut donc tabler sur au moins quatre à cinq mois d’attente.
Pour aller plus loin GTA 6 est disponible en France : tout savoir sur lancement du jeu phare de Rockstar
À 30 images par seconde, un ordinateur dispose de 33,3 millisecondes pour calculer et afficher chaque image ; à 60 images par seconde, ce budget temps tombe à 16,7 millisecondes. Si la carte graphique se charge de dessiner les décors à l’écran, c’est le processeur (CPU) qui orchestre toute la vie de Vice City : le trafic routier, les centaines de passants, la physique des véhicules et les réactions de la police.

Sur cette base matérielle, le jeu plafonne à 30 images par seconde en 1440p, et abaisser les options graphiques ne débloque pas une seule image supplémentaire.

articles.t: GTA 6 en serait à 45 millions d'exemplaires vendus, dont 75 % sur PS5, selon Alinea
articles.chapeau: Et déjà 4 milliards de dollars pour le jeu de tous les records
articles.txt:
Alors, ce premier week-end sur Grand Theft Auto VI , ça s'est bien passé pour vous ? Chez Take-Two, en tout cas, l'humeur doit être plutôt bonne pour un lundi. Selon de nouvelles estimations, le chiffre d'affaires du jeu de Rockstar Games aurait déjà passé le cap des 4 milliards de dollars en 4 jours.
Rappelons d'abord que, selon le premier communiqué officiel de Take-Two Interactive, GTA 6 avait enregistré 32,5 millions d'exemplaires en précommande et généré la bagatelle de 3,8 milliards de dollars au terme de sa journée de lancement, le 19 novembre. Aujourd'hui, c'est Alinea Analytics qui y va de ses estimations. Selon les calculs de l'entreprise, GTA 6 aurait atteint 44,9 millions d'exemplaires vendus aux consommateurs (donc sans inclure les exemplaires invendus des boutiques) au terme du week-end.
La PS5 représente 75 % de ces estimations de ventes (33,7 millions), contre 25 % pour la Xbox Series (11,2 millions). Quant au chiffre d'affaires, bien aidé par le succès de l'édition Ultimate à 100 dollars, il aurait donc franchi la barre des 4 milliards de dollars en 4 jours, dont 3 milliards de dollars dépensés par les joueurs PlayStation 5. À supposer que GTA 6 soit soumis au même prélèvement de 30 % que les autres titres, on parlerait donc déjà de 900 millions de dollars tombés dans la poche de Sony Interactive Entertainment.
Comme le note Alinea, ce chiffre d'affaires représente l'équivalent du box-office combiné des deux plus gros succès cinéma de l'été ( Spider-Man Brand New Day et L'Odyssée ). Pour trouver une comparaison avec la musique, c'est aussi le double de l'argent généré par les 149 concerts de la tournée Eras Tour de Taylor Swift entre mars 2023 et décembre 2024.
Toujours selon les estimations d'Alinea, 40,8 millions de joueurs se seraient connectés pour jouer à GTA 6 au cours de la journée du dimanche 22 novembre, dont 76 % sur PS5. Environ 20 % des acheteurs ont dépassé le cap des 20 heures de jeu.
Par ailleurs, les estimations géographiques montrent une forte domination du public américain. Sur les 33,7 millions d'exemplaires vendus sur PS5, 11,1 millions viennent des États-Unis (33 %). La France arrive en seconde place avec 3 millions de ventes (9 %), devant le Royaume-Uni (2,5 millions), l'Allemagne (1,7 million) et la Chine (1,6 million).
Juste pour bien comprendre ce que représentent ces 3 millions de ventes en France : d'ordinaire, le jeu le plus vendu dans l'Hexagone chaque année est EA Sports FC avec des ventes qui tournent autour de 1,5 million de copies pour l'ensemble de l'année. Ici, selon Alinea, GTA 6 aurait donc fait le double des ventes rien que sur PS5 en l'espace de quatre jours. Si on remonte jusqu'en 2013, Grand Theft Auto V était crédité de 1,9 million de ventes (sur PS3 et Xbox 360) entre sa sortie en septembre et le 31 décembre.
Enfin, voilà qui ne va pas arranger les affaires de Call of Duty, l'arrivée de GTA 6 aurait provoqué une chute particulièrement forte de l'audience de la franchise d'Activision. Et contrairement à Fortnite qui a récupéré ses joueurs petit à petit depuis le 19 novembre, Call of Duty ne montre aucun signe de récupération quatre jours plus tard. « La tendance observée ici correspond largement à ce que nous avions prédit il y a quelques semaines. Les poids lourds des jeux-service ont encaissé un coup immédiat avec GTA, mais ils ont rebondi parce qu'ils sont profondément ancrés dans les habitudes. Call of Duty fait figure d'exception ici, et Xbox devrait — honnêtement — s'inquiéter pour l'une de ses franchises phares », estime l'analyste Rhys Elliott.

'GTA 6' on PC: What we know about the PC release
articles.chapeau: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is here for console gamers, but remains one of the most-anticipated video games of all time on PC.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming , with limits).
GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.
An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially announced yet.
Despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's plans. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.
Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.
Console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.
A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents said they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.
However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.
Speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz , former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN , Ricchio said it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.
Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.
If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.
Grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.
The one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition , which launched simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.
A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one , despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting."
Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.
Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

Here’s how to open the secret portal and unlock Tommy Vercetti’s iconic blue Hawaiian shirt in GTA 6 .
YouTuber Memeio has discovered a major GTA 6 Easter egg just days after launch. According to creator, the secret quest starts at the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento, where flipping a switch and pressing a button makes the Malibu Club logo flash on a TV . From there, the puzzle sends players to 12 LPL substations scattered across Leonida.
The clues at the substations spell out “LIFE IS PASSING ME BY,” a cheat code from the original GTA: Vice City that sped up the in-game clock. After pressing the right buttons and pulling the right levers in order, you’ll receive a text from an unknown number that reads “U-235 REACTOR2 19-06.”

That message points to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station, where a purple portal opens between 7 PM and 6 AM in-game . Step through it as Jason and you’ll find yourself inside the Malibu Club, complete with PS2-style graphics and an appearance from Kent Paul. Once you return, you’ll unlock Tommy Vercetti’s blue Hawaiian shirt.
The switch sequence was discovered by Memeio, who shared it on X . Tommy’s shirt is a great reward, but my favorite part of the Easter egg is how Rockstar uses an old cheat code to make the whole thing work. “Life Is Passing Me By” used to make time move faster. More than two decades later, it’s the clue that sends you back to the Malibu Club.

articles.chapeau: Discover how workplace gaming culture, from LAN parties to GTA 6, builds team trust and belonging, even for employees who don't play.
articles.txt:
(Credits: South_agency/Getty) Grand Theft Auto VI arrived Nov. 19, 13 years after GTA 5 Opens a new window , and by now someone on your team has probably asked for launch day off. My former girlfriend took off every Assassin’s Creed release day, no questions asked.
Gallup found that only 30% of employees have a best friend at work Opens a new window , and those who do are seven times more likely to be engaged. Shared hobbies are one of the easiest ways those friendships start. I have experienced both sides: being the one who lugged a PC to the LAN party and being the PC to the LAN party and being the one who skipped the fantasy league. You don’t have to play to belong, but it helps to know how the game works.
Long before anyone preloaded GTA 6, my graduated classmates and I bonded over Doom. Someone would haul a tower PC into a friend’s basement, and by 9 p.m. a room full of us were hunting each other across a network we’d wired ourselves. StarCraft came next, and later World of Warcraft raids ran well past midnight. Keeping those games running taught us more about building PCs and networks than any class did, down to tuning graphics settings for one more frame per second.
READ MORE: Freshworks wants your help desk to run your whole IT shop
Once some of us landed IT jobs, the LAN parties followed us to work. It was a different time, before security was a major concern, and a manager’s OK was usually all it took to plug personal machines into the company network after hours. The most enthusiastic person on the team organized the nights. Nobody called it team building. It was fun, and the trust it built showed up months later, when a server went down at 2 a.m. and you already knew who would be by your side to fix it.
Coach Lancaster, a close friend and former co-worker, helped me see why those nights meant so much. He now teaches physical education and technology in New York City public schools, where he also coaches multiple sports. Lancaster holds a master’s degree in coaching, which is less about any one sport than about bringing different talent together and improving how a team performs. He told me shared hobbies build an unspoken trust, because people have lived through the same experience. As a certified life and executive coach, I’ve seen that trust form among leaders. Teams that have been through something together tend to work better side by side.
Lancaster said, “When I think back to games like Doom and StarCraft, what I remember is who I played with. Fantasy football does something similar at work. You might go all week saying ‘good morning’ to somebody in the hallway, and then one Monday you’re both laughing about the fantasy guy you left on the bench. As a coach, that matters to me. Once you’re comfortable talking to each other about the little things, it’s easier to ask for help or speak up when the team needs you.
The thing I watch for is who’s on the outside of the joke. If you need to know last night’s score to join the lunch table conversation, we’ve missed the point. I love a little trash talk, but everybody ought to feel like part of the team whether they play or not.”
Wharton management professor Nancy Rothbard, who studies friendship at work, has seen the same thing. “It’s the classic clique type of situation, like the high school cafeteria,” she told Knowledge at Wharton Opens a new window . The people inside the friendship group are fine. Everyone else can feel left out, even when nobody meant to leave them out.
I’ve been one of those people looking in. When the fantasy football league took over Monday mornings, I wasn’t in it, and some days it felt exclusive. Because of Lancaster’s advice, though, I understood what was happening. Nobody was shutting me out. They had a shared story, and I didn’t.

So I learned how much to chime in and when I was out of my league, literally. I’d ask who won, give a nod to whoever had a good week, and let them enjoy it. That small acknowledgment kept me in the conversation without pretending to care about the waiver wire. The same approach works for GTA 6. Ask a coworker what they think of the new map, and you’ll get a 10-minute answer from someone who now feels noticed.
From there, look for your own common ground. A lunch spot or a band you both like builds the same familiarity a game does. What people remember is the time you spent together, whatever you spent it on.

The group says it plans to release the missing executable for a leaked Xbox build on November 23. If the file works as claimed, it could accelerate unofficial PC emulation, though a playable version is not guaranteed.
Cyberleek, a hacking group or possibly an individual, has released what is said to be a development build of the Xbox version of GTA 6. The release came late last week; the leaked files and assets reportedly total 209GB.
Various sources have said the files are genuine. TweakTown reports that cybersecurity group VX Underground believes the leak is real and has theorized that Cyberleek obtained the build by compromising a Rockstar Games employee. The executable file that runs the game was missing from the build, and Cyberleek said it would release that file on November 23.
Cyberleek had previously threatened to release the full game. The group said the files would have been leaked earlier if its crypto coin had reached a market capitalization of $15 million; otherwise, it would release them on November 23.
Cyberleek claims that releasing the executable would let the community emulate GTA 6 within a week and run it at well over 30fps.
This community will have it [GTA 6] emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. [Cyberleek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.
The group added that if the Xbox build could not be made to work and “support holds”, it would try to obtain a PS5 build as a fallback, “most likely never required”.
Even if the executable appears today and the Xbox build works, community projects would still need to make an unofficial PC version playable. An early version could be unstable, crash-prone and affected by glitches. TechRadar also warns that unofficial builds carry risks: scammers are already distributing malware disguised as GTA 6 versions, and that activity could increase if the file is released.
The progress of emulation could put pressure on Rockstar to bring forward its official PC port, the article says. Rumors point to an early 2027 release, but the timing is unconfirmed.
If this [Cyberleek leak] is real, we're actually getting GTA 6 on PC before Rockstar even announces it. Maybe this finally forces them to move the official release up.

articles.txt:
Suivez LEBIGDATA.FR G o o g l e News Discover Ajouter comme source préférée Relu par Bastien L. , Rédacteur en chef
Attendre la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre était déjà pénible. Alors, espérer l’arrivée d’une éventuelle version PC que Rockstar n’a pas encore annoncée, je ne vous le fais pas dire.
Mais depuis quelques jours, les joueurs PC sont enthousiastes. Pourquoi ? Parce qu’une communauté de pirates travaille à adapter une version Xbox du jeu aux ordinateurs.
Le groupe en question est connu sous le nom de Cyberleek. Oui, le même groupe qui a diffusé des images de GTA 6 et menacé de diffuser le jeu avant sa sortie officielle .
Le 19 novembre 2026, Cyberleek a diffusé une archive de 209 Go présentée comme une version Xbox Series X|S de GTA 6.
Celle-ci contient notamment des textures, des modèles 3D, des effets sonores et des shaders. Ces derniers sont des programmes qui participent au rendu graphique du jeu.
En clair, une bonne partie des éléments nécessaires à la représentation de l’univers de GTA 6 serait déjà disponible. Mais il manque une pièce essentielle au puzzle : l’exécutable principal .
Ce fichier contient les instructions permettant de lancer le programme. Sans lui, même avec des centaines de gigaoctets de ressources, impossible de démarrer une partie.
Cyberleek a annoncé vouloir publier ce fichier le 23 novembre . Toutefois, ses précédentes promesses non tenues obligent à prendre cette annonce avec des pincettes. Pour l’instant, rien ne permet d’affirmer qu’une version pirate fonctionnelle est disponible.
Le choix de la version Xbox n’est pas anodin. La Xbox Series X utilise une architecture x86-64 , que l’on retrouve également dans les processeurs de nombreux ordinateurs.
Cela facilite certaines opérations d’adaptation. Les développeurs n’ont pas besoin de repartir entièrement de zéro pour comprendre comment le jeu fonctionne.
Par ailleurs, un développeur connu sous le pseudonyme NotRexed entreprend de le faire avec son projet open source , baptisé Leonida , récemment apparu sur GitHub .
Bon, techniquement, il ne s’agit pas de recréer le jeu, mais de travailler à partir de ses ressources existantes. Le développeur cherche notamment à adapter les éléments graphiques et les composants logiciels nécessaires pour permettre au jeu de fonctionner dans un environnement PC.
Et les premiers résultats de Leonida sont déjà visibles. Le projet a notamment traduit 26 503 shaders vers Vulkan , une technologie qui permet de gérer l’affichage graphique sur différentes configurations matérielles.
Il permet aussi d’extraire des modèles 3D, des textures et des fichiers audio présents dans les données récupérées. L’intelligence artificielle participe également à ce travail.
Des agents de programmation assistent certaines opérations, ce qui peut accélérer le traitement de nombreux fichiers. Mais même avec cette aide, adapter un jeu aussi complexe n’est pas une mince affaire.

articles.t: GTA 6 Story Leak: 6 L.A. Noire 2 Claims, 0 Confirmed
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 story leak matches reports, but L.A. Noire 2, San Francisco and 2030 remain unconfirmed by Rockstar. Six claims sorted as of Nov. 23.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A 2023 leak is back at the center of Rockstar Games chatter, and the trigger is the finished game. Players and outlets say the post got the story and ending of Grand Theft Auto VI right years before launch, which has pushed its other claim, that Rockstar’s next project is L.A. Noire 2, into the spotlight. GAMINGbible ran the theory on November 21 under a headline saying the GTA 6 ending confirms a long-standing theory, and followed with a second report on November 23.
Here is the part the headlines skip. Rockstar has not announced L.A. Noire 2, a San Francisco setting, a Zodiac Killer plot or any release window. Every outlet that covered the GTA 6 story leak says so, some in the opening lines and some near the bottom. We covered the first wave of the rumor in our earlier look at the L.A. Noire 2 leak . This piece asks a different question: what does a correct ending actually prove about a claim that cannot be checked yet?
The short answer is less than the excitement suggests. Below, we sort six claims into confirmed and unconfirmed, compare how six outlets framed the story, trace where the post came from, weigh the competing candidates for Rockstar’s next game, and offer five predictions. Everything is current as of November 23, 2026.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
The reporting converges on one chain of events. In 2023, an anonymous poster shared details about GTA VI and about what Rockstar would make afterward. Once the game reached PlayStation and Xbox, players compared the post with the finished story, found matches, and pointed back to the line about the studio’s next title. GAMINGbible’s November 23 report says the leaker “got so much right” that the next claim is hard to ignore, while also saying readers should take it with a pinch of salt because Rockstar has announced nothing.
The claim itself is short. The alleged next game is L.A. Noire 2. It would move from 1940s Los Angeles to San Francisco and follow a new detective chasing the Zodiac Killer. GAMINGbible adds that the post described the project as being in early development back then, with a 2030 target, and that it expected face-tracking technology to return in upgraded form. TechJuice, writing on the same day, put the 2030 window at roughly four years after GTA 6 and ended its piece by stating that every L.A. Noire 2 claim remains unconfirmed as of November 23, 2026.
Indiatimes ran the story on November 21 and updated it on November 23. Its summary adds a late-1960s period and a new protagonist rather than a return of the original game’s lead, and it states plainly that Rockstar has not announced the sequel, confirmed the Zodiac plot or validated the date. That is the consistent pattern across coverage. The framing is enthusiastic, the hedging is explicit, and no outlet claims a Rockstar source.
Dexerto’s November 21 report by Callum Doyle gives the cleanest provenance. The claims appeared on GTAForums in 2023, shared by a user named Shahanshah, who relayed a post from an anonymous 4chan user. That anonymous account also covered several GTA 6 story details. Players on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit went back through the post after launch and said its ending details match the final game. Dexerto also says the same source had earlier been credited with details Rockstar later confirmed before launch, including Jason and Lucia’s relationship and the game’s Criminal Profile system.
Dexerto quotes the L.A. Noire line directly. The post reads, “You’re not gonna believe me, but Noire 2. Set in San Fran. Zodiac killer.” It then says the game was “still in the very early stages of development, though, it’ll probably be 2030 when it comes out.” On the visuals, Dexerto quotes the post as saying the higher-ups were talking about doing the face scanning again but making it “insane,” with the goal of “the best looking game ever made.”
Note the chain. An anonymous 4chan poster wrote the original text. A GTAForums user relayed it. Players and outlets then summarized the relay three years later. None of those links is a named insider, an internal document or a verified Rockstar employee. A reader can check whether the post says what outlets say it says. A reader cannot check whether the poster ever had access to anything.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : une version pirate dès aujourd'hui ?
articles.chapeau: Quatre jours après la publication d'une build Xbox de GTA 6 par Cyberleek, un projet open source baptisé Leonida affirme avoir préparé tout ce qu'il faut pour faire tourner le jeu sur PC. Le seul problème est qu'il manque toujours le fichier qui lance le jeu. Certains affirment qu'il pourrait être publié dès le 23
articles.txt:
Recevez tous les soirs un résumé de l’actu importante avec Le Récap’
Si vous vous intéressez à l’émulation, vous avez forcément entendu parler du projet Leonida. Ce dépôt GitHub promet de transformer la version Xbox Series X de GTA 6 en un jeu PC natif et beaucoup de comptes sur les réseaux sociaux le présentent comme un portage quasiment terminé. Le développeur, qui s’est aidé de l’IA pour tout coder en seulement quelques heures, est convaincu que son logiciel permettra à des millions de joueurs PC de découvrir GTA 6 au moment où l’exécutable du jeu sera publié. Mais est-ce vraiment plausible ?
Le projet est sérieux, mais il ne peut pas démarrer le jeu. Cyberleek affirme qu’il va publier les fichiers manquants le 23 novembre, mais tout miser sur un compte qui veut faire fructifier sa cryptomonnaie est un pari osé. Beaucoup de fausses vidéos circulent sur les réseaux sociaux.
GTA 6 sur PC : entre la build Cyberleek et les extractions PS5, la pression s’accentue pour Rockstar GTA 6 pour Xbox a fuité, mais il est impossible de démarrer le jeu Le 19 novembre, jour de la sortie de GTA 6 , Cyberleek a mis en ligne par torrent une archive de 209 Go présentée comme la build Xbox 1.0.2.1 du jeu, datée de novembre 2026. Le jeu est a priori authentique, mais il n’est pas jouable. L’exécutable principal, celui qui lance le jeu et qui contient tout son code, n’a pas été publié par Cyberleek.
Sans lui, l’archive n’est qu’un immense stock de modèles 3D, de textures, de sons et de shaders. Certains s’amusent à extraire la carte ou les voitures, mais la build est injouable.
Black Friday : Proton Pass Plus à -60 % Jusqu’au 30 novembre, Proton Pass Plus est à 1,99 € par mois pendant 12 mois, soit 60 % de réduction ! Alias d’adresse mail illimités pour profiter des codes promo sans saturer votre boîte, mot de passe unique par site, coffre-fort chiffré. Bref, un Black Friday sans stress ! Sponsorisé En ce moment à 1,99€ par mois Leonida sur Github. // Source : Capture Numerama Le leaker Cyberleek, déjà à l’origine de fuites massives cet été, tient le même discours depuis jeudi : l’exécutable sortira ce lundi 23 novembre « sans condition » (ou plus tôt si son memecoin $CYBERLEEK atteint une certaine capitalisation). Le pirate promet aussi que la communauté pourra émuler le jeu « en une semaine », Et si la build Xbox ne suffit pas, il assure qu’il cherchera à obtenir une build PS5. Bref, Cyberleek veut nuire à Rockstar. Cyberleek, qui se fait passer pour un « pirate militant » , est une personnalité très controversée. Tout suggère que ses motivations sont surtout financières et qu’il ne faut pas lui faire confiance.
Rappel important : si l’émulation en tant que telle n’est pas illégale dans tous les pays, elle nécessite toujours d’utiliser sa propre copie du jeu. Ce que propose Cyberleek est illégal et utiliser une build provenant d’un leaker aux objectifs malveillants n’est pas une bonne idée. Take-Two va probablement tout faire pour combattre le projet et est dans son droit.
En attendant des nouvelles de Cyberleek, la sphère de l’émulation PC s’active. Le projet Leonida est apparu sur GitHub le 20 novembre. Son créateur, NotRexed, n’est pas un inconnu : il est l’un des développeurs de Hookshot, le projet qui a porté sur PC le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time sorti sur Switch 2 à peine un jour après sa sortie.
Le principe s’appelle la recompilation statique. Le processeur de la Xbox Series utilise la même architecture x86-64 qu’un PC : le code du jeu peut donc tourner tel quel, sans émulation, à condition de recréer autour de lui tout ce que la console lui fournit (son système, ses bibliothèques Microsoft, sa version de DirectX). Les shaders, ces petits programmes graphiques compilés pour la puce AMD de la console, doivent eux être traduits pour Vulkan.
Le projet revendique déjà la traduction des 26 503 shaders du jeu, l’export des modèles, des textures et des banques audio, un chargeur capable de lancer un exécutable de test et une couche graphique qui commence à dessiner sur Vulkan. Le rythme est sans précédent : plus de 8 600 modifications en trois jours, des dizaines de contributeurs et plus de 17 000 étoiles sur GitHub. Le projet ne cache pas son recours massif à l’IA : il a des consignes dédiées aux agents de code et demande de signaler toute contribution assistée.

articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the leaker behind earlier GTA 6 leaks, has reportedly released a near-complete Xbox build of the game and claims modders could get it running on PC within a week.
The main executable is missing . Cyberleek says it will release the file Monday, Nov. 23, or sooner if its cryptocurrency token reaches a $15 million market cap.
Cybersecurity group VX Underground examined the files and said it found game assets, which led it to believe the leak is genuine.
Modder OptiJuegos noted that the Xbox build is a GDK app that shares much of its architecture with Windows, which could make a port easier. Even so, no one has shown the files running as a complete game on PC, and some system files are also reportedly missing.
GTA 6 is currently out only on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date and has warned it may pursue legal action against illegal ports.

articles.t: GTA 6's story seemingly confirms leak revealing Rockstar's next game
articles.chapeau: Those leaks might have been onto something after all...
articles.txt:
Leaked details on GTA 6 prior to its launch have now been proven to be true, adding credibility to Rockstar Games' next rumoured title.
GTA 6 finally being out in the wild has inadvertently added credibility to leaks released prior to the game’s launch. Some of these leaks revealed Rockstar’s next planned game.
Before you jump to any conclusions, no, it’s not GTA 7 or Red Dead Redemption 3 – it might be better…
Back in 2023, an anonymous leaker took to gtaForums to drop fresh intel on GTA VI , and what would come after the game had launched.
Several story details were disclosed, such as Jason and Lucia’s past as well as some of the game’s multiple ending outcomes.
Having reviewed and beaten the game , I’m shocked by how accurate these leaks were, especially considering they’re from 2023.
Because the anonymous user got so much right, it makes what they had to say next all the more interesting; Rockstar Games’ next title will be L.A. Noire 2.
Obviously we need to take this with a pinch of salt as Rockstar hasn’t officially announced plans for its next title, but the leaker got so much right about GTA VI it’s a hard rumour to ignore.
The L.A. Noire sequel will apparently be set in San Francisco, so expect a different title if it does get revealed, and it will follow a new detective tracking down the Zodiac Killer. Again, take this with a pinch of salt as in the end it could be a fictional killer that’s simply inspired by the real-world events.
Additional info from the leaks says it’ll bring back the face-tracking technology from the previous game, but with vast improvements to make it “the best-looking game ever made.”
When the leak was first published, it said the game was in early development and would target a 2030 launch window, but that probably didn’t factor in the several delays GTA VI received prior to launch.
READ NEXT: Five free GTA 6 gifts that PlayStation users might have missed on PS5
While Rockstar Games fans would have probably expected another Red Dead Redemption game, or God forbid GTA 7, after the release of GTA VI , an L.A. Noire sequel is a much better idea.
GTA VI has been years in the making and whatever open-world Rockstar crafts next is going to take just as long, if not longer, as we move onto next-gen consoles like Xbox Project Helix and the PlayStation 6.
Something like L.A. Noire or even the long-awaited sequel to Bully is exactly the type of game we need next. It’d be an excellent bridge between the massive, open-world titles, in addition to just being games we all want to see.
Again, we need to take the leaks with a pinch of salt, as while they were on the money regarding GTA VI that doesn’t mean they’re correct about Rockstar’s next game. Fingers crossed, though…
